question: In the Saale-Holzland district, an independent candidate wanted to stand for the district administrator position. After his candidacy was shown support by the AfD, he and his family were threatened, which led him to withdraw his candidacy1.

In the light of the situation in Saale-Holzland and of the European Democracy Action Plan, doubts arise about how democratic integrity and candidates’ safety are being ensured against the backdrop of the Union's fundamental values and Treaties.
The action plan aims to strengthen the resilience of democracies in the Union, to promote free and fair elections, and to encourage measures against disinformation and manipulation to be taken. 1.

How does the Commission assess compliance with the Union’s fundamental values and the Treaties with regards to free and safe elections, particularly in the context of the European Democracy Action Plan and events such as in Saale-Holzland?

What steps is the Commission taking to ensure the safety of all candidates in view of the upcoming Parliament elections, and also to prevent similar cases of intimidation and threats of violence from affecting democratic processes in the Union?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.7.2024) Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/2829 on inclusive and resilient elections1, issued as part of the Defence of Democracy package on 12 December 20232, aims to promote high democratic standards for elections in the EU, supporting high turnout, inclusive participation, easy and equal exercise of electoral rights and resilient electoral processes.
To this end, it includes specific recommendations to encourage election integrity and fair campaigning.

Political parties and campaign organisations are encouraged to adopt campaign pledges and codes of conduct including refraining from manipulative behaviour that threatens or has the potential to negatively impact values, procedures and political processes, in particular producing, using or disseminating misleading or hateful content. This is also a concern of European citizens.

In a Eurobarometer survey in which respondents were asked to rate the most important aspects of free and fair electoral campaigns, the strongest responses concerned debates and campaigns avoiding hate speech, manipulation and lies. The Code of Conduct was signed by European political parties on 9 April 2024 following the recommendation issued by the Commission3.

The Commission works closely with the Member States’ competent authorities, including in Germany, to promote free and fair elections in the EU, and to support the exchange of best practices on elections, including in the framework of the European Cooperation Network on Elections4, with a thematic session on candidate safety in May 2024 to discuss ways to support candidates against harassment and disinformation.
